C0.quote: We analyse optimal voting weights in two-tier voting systems.
C0.note: Two-tier voting with weighted council votes; probabilistic model of votes and optimal weights. Borderline but about a voting procedure.

C1.quote: minimise the democracy deficit, i.e. the expected deviation of the council
C1.note: Optimal weights minimising expected deviation of council vote from popular vote is a performance objective (WD); probabilistic model analysis could also be OT.

C2.1.value: votes (voting configurations; votes X_λi of voters, council vote)
C2.1.quote: The vote of voter i ∈ {1, . . . , Nλ} in group λ will be denoted by Xλi.

C2.2.quote: Let the two voting alternatives be encoded as ±1, +1 for ‘aye’
C2.2.note: Binary yes/no votes (±1) on a proposal; does not fit RANK/APPR etc.

C2.3.quote: obeying the voters’ preferences which we do not model explicitly
C2.3.note: Preferences are mentioned but not modelled.

C2.4.quote: the votes cast are assumed to be deterministic and rational, obeying the voters’ preferences
C2.4.note: Votes obey preferences, no reason given; preferences not modelled separately. Also Section 9 mentions sincere voting only as a possible setting.

C3.1.note: Votes are random variables from the bias model; no analysis has voters misreporting. Section 9 mentions incentives to misrepresent only in passing.

C3.2.quote: obeying the voters’ preferences which we do not model explicitly
C3.2.note: Stated in words that votes obey preferences.

C3.3.note: No reason given for the claim that votes obey preferences.

C4.1.note: Input is binary vote; format is OTH, so applicability condition not met.

C5.1.quote: a measure of how well the council votes follow the public opinion
C5.1.note: Democracy deficit is a representation criterion: deviation of council vote from referendum; also minimised in formal results.

C5.2.quote: the votes cast are assumed to be deterministic and rational
C5.2.note: Deficit is evaluated on votes (input); paper states votes obey voters' preferences (IDS).

VOT.quote_behav: obeying the voters’ preferences which we do not model explicitly
VOT.note: Voters' votes are generated by exogenous random bias model; group representatives cast council vote by majority.

DES.note: Designer chooses weights to minimise deficit, but the designer's choice is an optimisation by the analyst, not an acting agent in the model; kept N.

C9.1.note: Claims in introduction/warm-up about real institutions (US Electoral College) and which weights to use. Only the introduction is cited since no separate conclusion claim of this kind was found.

C9.2.quote: this is the first theoretical justification of the formula that determines
C9.2.note: Needs that the probabilistic CBM (random bias, symmetric votes) describes real voting and that the democracy deficit is the right normative criterion; the latter is argued partly. The link of votes to preferences is stated only vaguely; the real-world applicability of the bias model is not established.
